content.title: About
content.content: Pupusa is a traditional Salvadoran dish consisting of a thick corn‑maize tortilla stuffed with meat, cheese, beans, or other fillings. The meat version typically contains finely chopped beef or pork seasoned with spices and onions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pupusas are cooked on a flat griddle called a “parilla”.
They are traditionally served with salsa, tomato sauce, and pickled cabbage “curtido”.
There are more than 30 regional filling variations, with meat being one of the most popular.
In 2015 UNESCO added pupusa to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list of El Salvador.
The dough is made from fermented corn masa, giving the dish its distinctive aroma.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat filling provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef and pork are rich in heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Corn masa offers complex carbs
items.content: Corn dough releases energy slowly, helping maintain satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and corn provide niacin, vitamin B6, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Unlike many fast‑food items, pupusa contains no added sugars.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If the filling is seasoned with soy sauce or extra salt, the dish can be high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Fatty meat increases saturated fat levels, potentially affecting cholesterol.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to corn masa.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Pupusas are calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pupusas are served hot, split in half. They can be dipped in salsa, sour cream, or guacamole. Often accompanied by rice, beans, and curtido.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked pupusas are best eaten within 2–3 days, stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator. They can be frozen for up to 2 months; before reheating, thaw and warm on a skillet or in the oven.
